clue.text: OT character before road accepted by most returning pilgrims

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so these words put one piece inside the other
returning means going back, so the trimmed word is read backwards
most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: HAJI (or hajji) is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca; the word also serves as a plural
ERE is a poetic word for before
MI stands for the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: A Bible figure walks ahead of a road taken by a band of pilgrims heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' trims HAJI to HAJ, 'returning' turns it to JAH, and 'accepted by' places EREMI inside it. OT is the Old Testament, the puzzle's double theme alongside Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremiah is one of the major prophets, with a book of the Old Testament bearing his name.

indicators.note: removing the top of a word in a down clue takes off its first letter

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: A bird has pecked the top off a rue plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Rue here is the verb meaning to be sorry, not the herb; in a down clue its top is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white wading heron.

clue.text: The badly fed, including supporter that isn't perceptive, utter obscenities

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the jumbled letters
badly signals that the letters of fed are rearranged

parts.note: a fan is a supporter of a team or star
someone blind cannot perceive by sight

explanation.surface: Underfed people with a dim-witted backer start cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eff and blind' is British slang for swearing, 'eff' standing in for a four-letter word; 'The badly fed' reads like hungry people, but 'badly' only signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom to eff and blind means to swear profusely, a slang phrase for cursing.

indicators.note: in places the abbreviations inside the name of the city

parts.note: Ilion (Ilium) is the Greek name for Troy
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A traveller in ancient Troy sees a mirage of America left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, something seen that is not really there.

clue.text: Quick visit causes leaderless country to prosper

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter of the country is dropped

parts.note: Thailand is a country in south-east Asia
to fare well is to do well or prosper

explanation.surface: A brief trip makes a nation without a head flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting followed at once by goodbye describes an encounter that is over almost as soon as it starts.

clue.text: Second group takes to getting drunk

parts.note: B is the second letter, as in B-grade or class B
a lot is a set or batch of items, a group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A second band of people takes to drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for very drunk.

definitions.meaning: a ... bee is one that buzzes, and to ... is to drone or buzz

explanation.walkthrough: Here OT is Oliver Twist rather than the Old Testament, the puzzle's playful double theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumble is both the pompous parish beadle of Dickens's novel and an old verb for a droning hum.

clue.text: OT sprayed Dettol over part of fower

indicators.note: over means covering, so the jumbled letters wrap round the flower part
something sprayed is scattered, so the letters of Dettol are rearranged

parts.note: the stamen is the pollen-bearing part of a flower (fower is the clue's slip for flower)

explanation.surface: Someone sprays disinfectant over a bit of a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprayed' rearranges the disinfectant's name into OLDTET, which 'over' wraps round the flower part. Dettol is a British antiseptic brand; 'fower' is the clue's slip for flower.
explanation.definitionFit: OT is the standard abbreviation for the first part of the Christian Bible.

indicators.note: made here means made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 7 down begins OLD

explanation.surface: A character from the book got the guard worried.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is OLD (from 7), GUARD and FRET together, twelve letters rearranged. OT is Oliver Twist here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Artful Dodger is the young pickpocket Jack Dawkins in Dickens's novel.

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so setter's is I am, I'M
a mode is a way or manner

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a way of living on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodest describes someone lacking modesty, given to bragging.

indicators.note: turn means the word is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: nuts means crazy, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A madman takes his turn to shock everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astound or stagger them.

definitions.meaning: a little royal person would be a princeling

explanation.definitionFit: Small royal is an old paper format, and read literally the phrase describes a minor or young member of a ruling family.

clue.text: Look up "green" (I knew about it) in OT

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the archaic phrase goes round the colour

parts.note: wist is an archaic past tense meaning knew
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone checks a colour in a book they already knew about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' with quotation marks looks like a word to define, but it is the heraldic colour; OT here means the Dickens novel rather than the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: OT abbreviates the title of Dickens's novel about a workhouse orphan.

clue.text: Has changed number held by fictional agent almost beyond the pale

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters of has are rearranged
held by means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: James Bond is the famous fictional secret agent
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone has changed a number kept by a spy, putting it nearly out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond the pale' sounds like outrageous behaviour, but here it describes a colour so pale it is close to white.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blond is a very light silvery-blond hair shade, so pale it nearly passes whiteness.

clue.text: Flat held by coach of League One club

indicators.note: held by means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a stage, as in stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach
even means level or flat

explanation.surface: A flat is owned by the coach of a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: League One is the third tier of English football; Stevenage FC played there. 'Flat' and 'coach' look like a home and a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a Hertfordshire town whose football club competed in English League One.

definitions.meaning: a single thing in a list is one entry
a couple who are romantically linked are said to be one

explanation.definitionFit: Item means a single article, and in slang a pair of lovers is called an item.

parts.note: airs are tunes, and those coming from the sky would be sung by birds

explanation.definitionFit: Birdsong is the musical calling of birds, melodies heard from the sky.

clue.text: OT character to rise at the Tate?

definitions.meaning: A son of Jacob in the Old Testament
put this name at the word Tate and it spells a verb meaning to float upwards

explanation.walkthrough: Tate looks like the London gallery, but it is a word to attach: LEVI then TATE makes levitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi is the patriarch of the priestly tribe; joined to Tate it forms the word for rising into the air.

clue.text: I make crosswords before going round with liqueur

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the setter's work sits inside the other word

parts.note: ante is Latin for before
to set is what a crossword setter does

explanation.surface: A crossword setter has a drink before going on a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

definitions.meaning: a contest between two directly is described this way
the English rendering of the French tete-a-tete, an intimate chat

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a one-on-one contest and translates the French for an intimate talk.

indicators.note: missing means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: tiffin is a light lunch, from Anglo-Indian usage

explanation.surface: A meal goes missing and a row breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel.

clue.text: OT character's hard work at home

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the character

parts.note: fag is British slang for a tiring chore
in means at home

explanation.surface: A character from the book works hard at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag in British slang is a tedious grind. OT is Oliver Twist here.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin is the old fence who runs a gang of child thieves in Dickens's novel.

clue.text: Dispute following river to delta in France

indicators.note: following means the dispute comes after the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
to argue is to dispute

explanation.surface: A quarrel follows the river down to a French delta.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camargue is the marshy delta of the Rhone in southern France.

definitions.meaning: The third king of Judah in the Old Testament
similes are often framed with the words as and a, as in as dead as a dodo

explanation.definitionFit: Asa is a biblical king, and split in two it gives the words that introduce many comparisons.

indicators.note: dance signals that the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Seals sing or dance in a show.

definitions.meaning: to ... to a place is to go there
to ... something is to fix it

explanation.definitionFit: Repair means both betaking oneself somewhere and fixing what is broken.

clue.text: Visual aids obtained with few pounds in Gateshead

parts.note: something weighing few pounds is light
read as Gate's head, the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: Seeing aids come from a few quid in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead, a town opposite Newcastle, is read as Gate's head, the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting helps people to see, providing illumination.
